packet.headline_seed: Musk says US military suicide drones used Starlink in violation of SpaceX rules
packet.description_seed: SpaceX and the Pentagon have been bickering about the price of using Starshield satellite service during the Iran war, according to a Reuters report published today. It appears that SpaceX asked the military for more money after it started using satellite terminals on "kamikaze" attack drones in Iran. SpaceX CEO Elon Musk claimed the Reuters report is wrong. But Musk also said the military drones initially used the commercial Starlink service instead of the government-specific network, in violation of Starlink's terms of service. Musk blamed the violation on the contractor that built the drones for the government. The Reuters report, based on Pentagon documents and interviews with sources familiar with the pricing talks, said that SpaceX recently asked the military to pay $25,000 for Starshield access on each kamikaze drone. The Pentagon, which previously paid $5,000 for each connection, objected to the price hike but ultimately agreed to pay it, according to Reuters. Read full article Comments

SpaceX and the Pentagon have been bickering about the price of using Starshield satellite service during the Iran war, according to a Reuters report published today. It appears that SpaceX asked the military for more money after it started using satellite terminals on “kamikaze” attack drones in Iran. SpaceX CEO Elon Musk claimed the Reuters report is wrong. But Musk also said the military drones initially used the commercial Starlink service instead of the government-specific network, in violation of Starlink’s terms of service. Musk blamed the violation on the contractor that built the drones for the government.

The Reuters report, based on Pentagon documents and interviews with sources familiar with the pricing talks, said that SpaceX recently asked the military to pay $25,000 for Starshield access on each kamikaze drone. The Pentagon, which previously paid $5,000 for each connection, objected to the price hike but ultimately agreed to pay it, according to Reuters. While the $25,000 charge is a monthly fee for the satellite connection provided to a satellite terminal, the terminals are being used with drones that only make one-way trips before hitting targets and detonating on impact. Starshield is a network for government entities and is based on Starlink technology. Musk wrote in an X post today that the “Reuters article is false.” But in the very same post, he seemed to confirm a dispute over how the military used SpaceX satellite technology.

“They made improper use of the Starlink civilian system for military purposes. Direct violation of terms of service,” Musk wrote today, seeming to indicate that the military used the commercial Starlink system when it should have been using Starshield. Musk said later that the drones were configured incorrectly by a military contractor. “There is a US government arm of SpaceX called Starshield, which has a different set of satellites than Starlink, which is for civilian use. The company that makes the suicide drones incorrectly used the civilian system, instead of the Starshield,” Musk wrote. The Pentagon “denied any violation of its agreement with SpaceX,” according to Reuters. Starshield terminals sold by SpaceX to the military can connect both to the commercial Starlink satellite constellation and Starshield, the Reuters article said.

[Lähde: Ars Technica]
SpaceX and the Pentagon have been bickering about the price of using Starshield satellite service during the Iran war, according to a Reuters report published today. It appears that SpaceX asked the military for more money after it started using satellite terminals on “kamikaze” attack drones in Iran.

SpaceX CEO Elon Musk claimed the Reuters report is wrong. But Musk also said the military drones initially used the commercial Starlink service instead of the government-specific network, in violation of Starlink’s terms of service. Musk blamed the violation on the contractor that built the drones for the government.

The Reuters report, based on Pentagon documents and interviews with sources familiar with the pricing talks, said that SpaceX recently asked the military to pay $25,000 for Starshield access on each kamikaze drone. The Pentagon, which previously paid $5,000 for each connection, objected to the price hike but ultimately agreed to pay it, according to Reuters.

While the $25,000 charge is a monthly fee for the satellite connection provided to a satellite terminal, the terminals are being used with drones that only make one-way trips before hitting targets and detonating on impact.

Starshield is a network for government entities and is based on Starlink technology. Musk wrote in an X post today that the “Reuters article is false.” But in the very same post, he seemed to confirm a dispute over how the military used SpaceX satellite technology.

“They made improper use of the Starlink civilian system for military purposes. Direct violation of terms of service,” Musk wrote today, seeming to indicate that the military used the commercial Starlink system when it should have been using Starshield.

Musk said later that the drones were configured incorrectly by a military contractor. “There is a US government arm of SpaceX called Starshield, which has a different set of satellites than Starlink, which is for civilian use. The company that makes the suicide drones incorrectly used the civilian system, instead of the Starshield,” Musk wrote.

The Pentagon “denied any violation of its agreement with SpaceX,” according to Reuters. Starshield terminals sold by SpaceX to the military can connect both to the commercial Starlink satellite constellation and Starshield, the Reuters article said.

The drones in question are part of the Low-cost Uncrewed Combat Attack System (LUCAS), which was made by defense contractor Spektreworks. We contacted Spektreworks today

payload.title: Musk kiistää Reutersin tiedot mutta sanoo Yhdysvaltain droonien käyttäneen Starlinkia sääntöjen vastaisesti
payload.summary: Elon Muskin mukaan Yhdysvaltain armeijalle valmistetut hyökkäysdroonit käyttivät aluksi siviilikäyttöön tarkoitettua Starlink-järjestelmää, vaikka sotilaskäyttöön on erillinen Starshield-palvelu. Reutersin mukaan SpaceX ja Pentagon ovat kiistelleet yhteyksien hinnasta.
payload.content:
Elon Musk sanoo, että Yhdysvaltain armeijalle valmistetut kertakäyttöiset hyökkäysdroonit käyttivät aluksi SpaceX:n siviilikäyttöön tarkoitettua Starlink-satelliittipalvelua tavalla, joka rikkoi palvelun käyttöehtoja. Samalla Musk kiisti Reutersin raportin paikkansapitävyyden, vaikka hänen omat viestinsä näyttävät vahvistavan, että SpaceX:n satelliittiteknologian käytöstä sotilasdroonien yhteydessä on syntynyt kiista.

## Kiista Starlinkin ja Starshieldin käytöstä

Reutersin raportin mukaan SpaceX ja Pentagon ovat käyneet erimielistä keskustelua Starshield-satelliittipalvelun hinnoittelusta Iranin sodan aikana. Starshield on hallituksille tarkoitettu palvelu, joka perustuu Starlink-teknologiaan mutta on erotettu siviilikäyttöisestä Starlinkista.

Musk kirjoitti X-palvelussa, että Reutersin artikkeli on väärä. Samassa yhteydessä hän kuitenkin sanoi, että drooneissa oli käytetty Starlinkin siviilijärjestelmää sotilaallisiin tarkoituksiin. Muskin mukaan kyse oli suorasta käyttöehtojen rikkomuksesta.

Myöhemmin Musk tarkensi, että droonit oli hänen mukaansa määritetty väärin niitä valmistaneen sotilasurakoitsijan toimesta. Hänen mukaansa Yhdysvaltain hallinnolle tarkoitettu SpaceX:n Starshield olisi ollut oikea järjestelmä, ei siviilikäyttöinen Starlink.

## Reuters: Pentagon vastusti hinnankorotusta

Reutersin mukaan SpaceX pyysi hiljattain Yhdysvaltain armeijalta 25 000 dollarin kuukausimaksua Starshield-yhteydestä kutakin niin sanottua kamikaze-droonia kohden. Aiemmin Pentagon oli raportin mukaan maksanut 5 000 dollaria yhteydeltä.

Raportin mukaan Pentagon vastusti hinnankorotusta mutta suostui lopulta maksamaan sen. Reuters perustaa tietonsa Pentagonin asiakirjoihin ja hinnoitteluneuvotteluista tietäviin lähteisiin.

Erimielisyyttä korostaa se, että kyseiset droonit on kuvattu kertakäyttöisiksi aseiksi, jotka lentävät kohteeseensa ja räjähtävät osuessaan. Reutersin mukaan maksu koski silti satelliittiterminaalin kuukausittaista yhteyttä.

Pentagon kiisti Reutersille rikkoneensa sopimustaan SpaceX:n kanssa. Reutersin mukaan SpaceX:n armeijalle myymät Starshield-päätteet voivat muodostaa yhteyden sekä kaupalliseen Starlink-satelliittijärjestelmään että Starshieldiin. Tämä voi selittää, miksi teknologian käytöstä on syntynyt kiista palvelun ehtojen, sopimusten ja hinnoittelun rajapinnoilla.
